articles.title: The 10 Best SNES Games to Play on Nintendo Switch Online
articles.summary: The Super Nintendo Entertainment System has one of the finest game catalogs of any console ever released, and there's a strong selection of 77 games available on Nintendo Classics as part of Nintendo Switch Online.
body: But it doesn't really matter, because you will, of course, find many of Nintendo's own games — and these represent an incredible golden age for the studio, when Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka's teams were pumping out masterpiece after masterpiece. It's one of the best runs any game developer has ever had, a time of perfection between the innovation of the NES before and the bold leap into 3D with the N64 that came after.
Here are the 10 best SNES games you can play on Nintendo Classics.

Nintendo loves to put together oddball game-and-accessory bundles, and in 1992 it sold a mouse for the SNES with this delightful art creation suite. There are funny minigames, brilliant tunes, authentic Nintendo sprites to use, as well as drawing, animation, and music creation suites. You'll need a USB mouse to play it on Switch, but Switch 2 owners can use the Joy-Con 2 in mouse mode.

articles.title: Netflix Just Quietly Added the Worst Vampire Series of 2025
articles.summary: AMC brought its adaptation of Anne Rice’s Interview with the Vampire to Netflix in 2024, kicking off a deal to give the streaming service access to its interconnected Immortal Universe.
body: The third and weakest show in the Immortal Universe arrives on Netflix on Aug. 23, and while the premise sounds compelling, you’d be better off skipping it. Talamasca: The Secret Order is the one series that isn’t directly adapting Rice’s books, instead taking a deep dive into the secret society whose members play a part in both The Vampire Chronicles and Lives of the Mayfair Witches. Much like the Watchers in Highlander and Buffy: The Vampire Slayer, Talamasca members study immortals, vampires, and witches. They also often have their own psychic abilities.

In an interview ahead of Talamasca ’s premiere in October 2025, series creator John Lee Hancock said he wanted to pay tribute to the tense spy stories of John le Carré, which is why he set the show in London. Anyone who wants to watch six episodes that really evoke le Carré’s novels should check out a season of Slow Horses on Apple TV. Seasons of Talamasca and Slow Horses run the same length, but Talamasca feels so much longer since it lacks the clever twists and compelling characters that make for a good thriller.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaker Releases More Gameplay Videos Despite Rockstar Owner Take-Two's Microsoft and Discord Subpoenas
articles.summary: The alleged GTA 6 leaker has released two further gameplay videos despite Rockstar owner Take-Two's subpoenas requesting identifying information from Microsoft and Discord.
body: The ‘CyberLeek’ person or group released two new videos today, August 22, one showing more supercar gameplay and an armed robbery, the other strip club gameplay. The latter appears to taunt Take-Two and Rockstar by showing a snippet of a cutscene in which a character says they need to take "a leak." This is the second cutscene to emerge this week, and there is growing concern that the leaker has access to a build of the game and may post significant story spoilers.
These new videos are the seventh and eighth to leak this week. And, like all the others, they advertise the ‘CyberLeek’ memecoin as part of what is widely considered to be a crypto scheme.

On August 20, Take-Two issued Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) subpoenas in a federal court requesting information from both Microsoft and Discord as part of its hunt for the leaker or leakers behind the recent spate of GTA 6 gameplay videos. Take-Two wants identifying information associated with user accounts that were members of a number of Discord servers, including one relating to Australian GTA content creator Matthew "Matt" Judge, aka DarkViperAU. Judge has denied any wrongdoing.

articles.title: The 5 Best Sci-Fi Movie Quotes of the Decade So Far
articles.summary: There are still a few years left in the 2020s, but it’s already been a fantastic decade for science fiction movies. The Dune films are likely the biggest highlight, as director Denis Villeneuve has finally brought the proper scale to Frank Herbert’s novels from the 1960s.
body: Of course, a huge part of the success of these films has been their scripts, which is why I decided to take a crack at figuring out the best sci-fi quotes of the decade thus far. There are a lot of good ones to choose from and plenty of room for debate. And surely, as the 2020s advance, at least a couple of these quotes will be eclipsed by others. But for now, these five are the best I could find.

The line is absurd on its face, but Pattinson delivers it with hilarious understatement, like someone complaining about bad weather. Mickey 17 is a very good film, largely because of writing like this.

23 years after the release of the 2002 zombie thriller 28 Days Later, director Danny Boyle and screenwriter Alex Garland returned with the follow-up 28 Years Later. With so many zombie movies out there, it might be hard to imagine anyone finding new ground to explore, but Boyle and Garland did exactly that with the wholly original character of Dr. Ian Kelson, played by Ralph Fiennes.

articles.title: After 49 Years, It's Officially the End of an Era for Star Wars
articles.summary: Ryan Gosling is known for enjoying a good jacket, and several of his characters wear outerwear that makes him stand out amongst the crowd. Even scatterbrained genius Ryland Grace from Project Hail Mary rocked an effortlessly cool sweater-jacket combo that made him the belle of the apocalypse.
body: Gosling’s character, Kade Auberon, was officially introduced to audiences at the annual D23 event in Anaheim, California, alongside several other new Star Wars announcements. When the trailer inevitably leaked online soon after, fans were drawn to Gosling’s jacket — specifically the symbol stitched across it and what it could mean for the future of Star Wars and/or the Rebel Alliance.

When George Lucas’s Star Wars first hit the silver screen in 1977, nobody could have predicted the iconic starbird plastered on X-Wing helmets and jackets would remain such a pivotal symbol of the franchise almost half a century later. Its iconography has changed slightly over the years, with Star Wars: Rebels revealing its in-universe origin as Sabine Wren's work. No matter how much time has passed, the symbol remains a perfect representation of the fight for freedom in an oppressive galaxy, from the Rebel Alliance in the original trilogy to the Resistance in the Disney-era sequels.
However, the meaning behind that symbol may be changing, if Ryan Gosling’s Starfighter jacket is any indication.

articles.title: Metal Gear Solid 4: The Flawed Masterpiece Kojima Didn't Want to Make
articles.summary: With Metal Gear Solid 4 finally arriving on modern consoles thanks to Master Collection Vol. 2, we take a look back at the game's legacy. Was it really just a big cutscene, or is it Kojima's masterpiece?
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Charlie Lopresto, who believes that love can bloom, even on a battlefield. He first encountered Metal Gear Solid on a demo disc from Pizza Hut and has since completed three hundred missions in VR– the kind that’s indistinguishable from the real thing.

Like Old Snake, Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots is a fossil. A genetic dead-end of gaming evolution, the unhinged and overflowing masterpiece that barely left a mark on the artform. Despite its commercial and critical success, MGS4 is rarely regarded as top tier Metal Gear. But is that actually fair?

Trapped on dead console hardware for the better part of its hard life, thanks to the new Master Collection Vol. 2 it’s finally possible for everyone to experience MGS4, from series diehards who first fired it up in 2008 to people completely new to Metal Gear who have absolutely no idea what they’re in for.

All of them will reckon with the many, many questions MGS4 brings to mind, like: Will we ever see a game like this again? Why did we stop talking about it? And, perhaps most importantly: MGS4 is really good, isn't it?

articles.title: Can the Epic Games Store turn things around? 'I don't see how they can recover at this point,' says Newzoo analyst
articles.summary: Back in February Epic Games told us about its plan to overhaul the Epic launcher, with an update in June mentioning it would start up five times faster on average. That technical overhaul will apparently be accompanied by changes to the storefront including personalized game recommendations…
body: "I don't really see how they can turn that around," Rosier says, "because Steam has become so inevitable. The Epic Games Store, they get players by giving free games, but people just go, they log in, they get the free games, they don't even play them. You know, it's almost like collecting games rather than actually playing them."

On a sample size of one I am the person who actually plays some of the free games I've been given by Epic over the years, and without that program I probably wouldn't have tried Guardians of the Galaxy, Ghostwire: Tokyo, Vampyr, Control, Assassin's Creed Syndicate, or Kardboard Kings. But whether most people play them or not, it's telling that a free giveaway can actually boost sales on Steam, as it did for Blood West, thanks to players not wanting to split their library.

"The challenge I think Epic is facing is that they try to win everywhere in the past few years," Rosier says. "They try to win against Steam, they try to win against Apple, against Google Play, and probably they run out of steam on where they cannot fight all these battles at the same time."

articles.title: Ultra Graphics Settings Are a Scam: Why High Is Good Enough, if Not Better, for Most Players
articles.summary: Most games don’t actually need to be played at Ultra settings to look good. They don’t even need it to look great. To prove it, I turned down the settings in a bunch of great-looking games to see how much difference it really makes.
body: I’m a privileged gamer. As a hardware reviewer, over the years I’ve been sent top-tier CPUs and graphics cards, letting me bounce from one flagship to the next. That’s made me lazy at game settings. I often just set the game at whatever the maximum “Ultra” setting is and get on with playing. But by doing so, I’ve just been playing into the marketing hype – and leaving a lot of performance on the table, it turns out.

I’ve been able to ignore graphics settings for so long due to a mix of low-demand game selection and high-end hardware. As I said, my current system is powerful, but I also mostly play older sim games and lighter indies.

With an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D and PowerColor Red Devil RX 7900 XTX, I have one of the fastest gaming CPUs on the market and the fastest graphics card AMD has ever made. It’s not quite an RTX 5080 or RTX 5090, so it’s not really designed with Ultra Path Tracing in mind, but it’s not a million miles away either. It’s more than capable of running almost any game at Ultra settings, at 4K, and sometimes even with ray tracing enabled.
That’s especially true once you throw in FSR upscaling and a little frame generation to smooth things out.
points: Most games don’t actually need to be played at Ultra settings to look good.
To prove it, I turned down the settings in a bunch of great-looking games to see how much difference it really makes.

articles.title: Modern Warfare 4 beta's first update is live, adding a new map, mode, and toned-down footsteps
articles.summary: Infinity Ward has deployed the first proper update to the Modern Warfare 4 beta, addressing a chunk of the feedback from the beta's opening day, including footstep audio, weapon lethality, and map voting.
body: "We heard you loud and clear on the footstep volume, so we've adjusted things downward for today," the studio said in its official patch notes blog post. As a result, enemy footstep and gear audio have had both their volume and audible range reduced.
Time-to-kill has also been tuned down on some weapons, with the ISO Nightshade SMG and Oris 8.6 marksman rifle both seeing their damage ranges and headshot multipliers reduced.
Infinity Ward says these are just the first adjustments and more changes are coming as it continues reviewing feedback and data.

A new map, Cachette, and a new mode, Inflation, have also joined the multiplayer rotation. Inflation tasks players with eliminating enemies and defeating HVT operators to collect cash, with the richest players becoming marked targets for everyone else to hunt. Cachette's addition also means there are now enough maps in the pool for map voting to be switched on, something Infinity Ward said needed four total maps to work properly.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker's console modes top out at 40fps, with no 60fps option at launch
articles.summary: New console gameplay from developer Rebel Wolves and publisher Bandai Namco has confirmed The Blood of Dawnwalker won't offer a 60fps mode on PS5 or Xbox Series X/S when it launches next month.
body: Two graphics modes are planned across both consoles: a Quality Mode targeting 30fps at dynamic 4K, and a Balanced Mode targeting 40fps at dynamic 4K.
PS5 Pro will hit the same frame rates and resolution, but with what's being described as enhanced visual quality across both modes.

The absence of a 60fps option, even on higher-end hardware, has left some fans hoping for a post-launch performance patch, with others saying they'd have preferred a lower-resolution 60fps mode over a 4K cap at 40fps.

"60 fps on Pro? Cmon guys," commented one on YouTube. Another said: "It’s 2026, 60 fps is the bare minimum at this point". Some fans believe a 60fps patch has been confirmed, but we're struggling to find confirmation – we'll update if/when we hear more.

articles.title: Compulsion Games' buyout is complete, so now Microsoft won't get a cut if you buy South of Midnight
articles.summary: South of Midnight was one of 2025's seemingly innumerable highlights—in their 83% review, evergreen writer Andrea Shearon called it "a Deep South delight drenched in superstition and pain." If you've been holding off but nonetheless rooting for the award-winning studio behind it, Compulsion Games…
body: After rumors of closure came in the wake of Xbox's most recent layoff-heavy bloodbath, Compulsion announced it'd be leaving Microsoft instead and pursuing other partnerships. On Thursday, CEO Guillaume Provost explained to GamesBeat that "the management buyout is complete and that it owns its original intellectual property games again, as Microsoft has transferred the IP back to Compulsion Games," according to the article. "Provost said management has acquired the studio and staff as well."

Granted, if you happened to be avoiding games by Microsoft-owned studios because of the BDS boycott protesting the roles of various corporations in Israel's ongoing genocide of Palestinians, this particular game and others like it were already excepted by some advocates. No Games For Genocide named it as a possible exception due to its indie-like production scale and "themes of black liberation" in its FAQ, saying "it’s worth putting our time, energy and efforts into building mass boycotts for the larger titles."
